newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-ICI Australia sees more improvement.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-ICI Australia sees more improvement.

text.p: ICI Australia Ltd said on Wednesday it remained positive about its second half results.
"Directors remain positive that improvements achieved in the first half will continue," the company said in a statement accompanying results for the first half ended March 31.

The company, 62.4 percent owned by Imperial Chemical Industries Plc, reported a net profit of A$110.7 million for the six months to March 31, up from A$92.6 million a year earlier. The 19.5 percent increase in net profit was struck on steady sales of A$1.69 billion.

"The company's (annual) result will remain dependent on the leel of activity in the Australian economy, particularly the housing and construction sector and on the strength of international plastic and chemical prices," ICI Australia said.
"The company will continue its strategy of creating value for shareholders by growing the profitable businesses in Australia and developing opportunities in Asia," it said.
"A strong focus is also being maintained on improving world competitiveness of the business portfolio with projects completed last year now starting to deliver results," it said.
ICI Australia said the result for the half year reflected mixed trading conditions in the Australian economy.

"The strong Australian and New Zealand currency had an adverse effect on businesses linked to export markets and was also detrimental for businesses competing with imported products," the company said.
"There was, however, some relief from high raw material prices in a number of areas," it said.
ICI Australia said its crop care business continued to perform strongly. Fertiliser markets also remained strong although international prices started to fall recently, it said.
In chemicals, trading conditions continued to be difficult.
"Increased raw materials costs and pressure on prices reduced margins," it said.

The company said its explosives business performed strongly in Australia and the Asia Pacific region. However, demand in the plastics sector was lower across all sectors, resulting in lower prices and volumes.
The consumer products division improved performance, reflecting higher sales volume by the Dulux paint division and a lower cost base, ICI Australia said.
The company said its financial position remained strong with gearing at 20 percent and interest cover at 12 times.
Capital expenditure for the period including acquisitions totalled A$137 million, down from A$194 million a year earlier.
ICI Australia shares were up 71 cents at A$12.80 at midday.
